topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and sets the learning outcomes for the lecture.

topics.label: Traditional cancer therapies, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional non-targeted interventions—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic drugs—and the physiological challenges and resistance mechanisms associated with them.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies designed to exploit inherent defects in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell-cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair pathway mutations.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale for inhibiting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and detail the molecular mechanisms through which cancer cells develop resistance to small-molecule kinase inhibitors.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail therapeutic approaches that use engineered monoclonal antibodies to disrupt receptor signaling or deliver cytotoxic payloads specifically to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and methods to harness the immune system against cancer using checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific engagers, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Overarching challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broad perspectives on cancer mortality trends, treatment personalization, and the ongoing ethical and clinical challenges in cancer management.
